messages:
Nina (PM): Drafting a lightweight migration playbook for private/VPC tenants. Key questions: pin semantics for compliance, minimal benchmark bar, and whether we require shadowing. Keeping it simple.
Omar (Product Lead): For private tenants, default should be hard-pin opt-out. Many require strict model consistency. But offer soft-pin as opt-in for customers who accept fallback.
Ivy (Eng Runtime): Implementation note: hard-pin means routing layer will NOT fallback automatically; we need a warm-standby requirement or customers risk outages.
Renee (Solutions): Sales asks for a documented exceptions flow for hard-pin extension beyond TTL. Suggest: SOW + product signoff + ticket in system.
Kai (SRE): From ops: require warm-standby for hard-pin. Also require a 48h shadow run in the tenant's environment (shadow responses logged) before cutover. Shadowing should be configurable to avoid PII capture if customer forbids it.
Nina (PM): Proposed minimal benchmarks for private: functional correctness smoke (customer-provided prompt set pass rate >= 90%) and perf: p95 latency within 2x their historical baseline.
Omar (Product Lead): Migration incentive: one-time migration engineering session for tenants > $50k ARR; for smaller tenants, give $1k credit.
Ivy (Eng Runtime): We'll add feature flags: pin_mode (hard/soft), require_warm_standby, enable_shadowing. Also add drift telemetry during shadowing.
Kai (SRE): Rollback triggers: sustained error-rate > 0.5% for 15m OR customer-provided quality metric drop > 6% on their gold prompts. If triggered, manual rollback since hard-pin may prevent auto-fallback.
Renee (Solutions): I'll write the exceptions process and sample contract language.
Nina (PM): Owners: Nina -> playbook doc + comms; Ivy -> flags + telemetry; Kai -> runbook + rollback checklist; Renee -> exceptions docs. Target: finalize by EOD next Thu.
Omar (Product Lead): Thanks. Post draft in #docs and ping me for approval.
